purpose: Safety-oriented period-bin validation threshold policy to reduce historical long-period (>100 d) candidate dismissals in the same four-feature forest. Report false-positive tradeoff, balanced accuracy, and all negative outcomes. No guarantee of improvement, no physical exoplanet confirmation.
development_motivation: Previously examined seed-12600 long-period group: RF labeled-candidate recall 44/71 while logistic 66/71, but the logistic let many more historical false-positive labels through. This is explicitly an after-the-fact method-development idea.
evaluation: GroupShuffleSplit by KIC host, exactly like ml_screening.split_by_star, 20% distinct-star test, 25% of remaining distinct-star validation. Never tune on test labels. Host sets do overlap ACROSS seeds so split results are not independent evidence.

baseline.threshold: ONE global validation candidate recall>=0.90 cutoff

new_method.fallback_if_fewer: Use the original global validation threshold for that bin
new_method.missing_period: Use the original global validation cutoff, no excluded test rows

primary_scientific_endpoint: Difference in balanced accuracy on TEST signals with period >=100 days, period-bin policy minus global-threshold policy, for predeclared first seed 14000.
secondary_measures: Long-period candidate recall and false-positive rate, with denominators and star-clustered uncertainty.
Overall balanced accuracy and false-negative/false-positive counts.
Per-bin counts, cutoff values and fallback logic.
Each of the ten overlapping grouped-host split results without pooling p-values.
No automatic human-review intervention or claim of more confirmed planets.

stats.interpretation: Even any low p value here is a data-development sensitivity analysis, NOT truly independent confirmation; original NASA catalog, baseline and original long-period difficulty already inspected.
stats.multiple_testing: One primary long-period balanced-accuracy contrast; other endpoints descriptive. All results must be retained regardless of direction.

limitations: The catalog's previous Robovetter candidate/false-positive labels are not confirmed physical planets.
Fewer long-period observations and low transit count can make faint planets harder; no direct light-curve completeness metric estimated.
Improving recall can also increase false-positive candidate alerts; a threshold movement is NOT intrinsic classifier skill improvement.
The method was conceived after viewing a weakness in prior split, so the reported new seeded folds are not an entirely independent scientific cohort.
When score rankings are unchanged, ROC AUC cannot improve: only operational decision thresholds move.
